scope: Proposition 8.4 (Wide-interval improvement) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 124. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the finite-narrowness parent data of Section 8.2: the joint caps, conditional palette domination at fine point and path states, and the true Qs graph lists. The observable X may be the native signal or any other bounded quadratic-along-lines signal with these data. At scales s, s + u, s + c2, put a = as, a1 = aN−u , a2 = aN−c2 . Suppose that simultaneous projected labels Φ, Φ1, Φ2 of the type constructed above, including their mass bounds, occur on dense mass and use the same α’s. Let βmin, βmax be their smallest and largest interval scales. Assume 0 < c2 < (1 − d)u/4 and βmax ≤ Kgs, bs/βmin + hsβmax/βmin ≤ N−(Cd+3)u , Cd = 10/(1 − d), up to subpower factors, with common scale exponents. Take all comparison meshes, including the intercept mesh χ, sufficiently fine in fixed powers relative to these widths and hs, bs, a1, so the transverse evaluation errors are negligible even at width a1. Then some true Q = Qs admits a quadratic predictor in the full base (t, Z, Y ) for X, of error Ka2 throughout its block on assigned trajectories, carrying original active mass at least qsνQ(a2/a)d /K. Here νQ is the full trajectory assignment weight.
